tytul: Ginger and lemon in honey: why there is no recipe here
wstep: There is no recipe here for fresh ginger and lemon kept in honey.

ostrzezenia.tekst: According to Oregon State University Extension, covering food with honey does not preserve it: lab trials found bacteria growing where the food meets the honey.

Oregon State University Extension limits high-moisture, low-acid ingredients, such as fresh garlic or herbs, to no more than 15% of a honey infusion by weight, using hot infusion only, with the honey kept above 140°F (60°C). After the infusion, the hot honey is strained to remove all pieces, so this method does not keep ginger or lemon in the honey.
Do not give honey or products made with honey to infants under 1 year of age.
The Polish National Centre for Nutrition Education (NCEŻ) lists honey among the foods an infant should avoid because of the risk of poisoning.

akapity: The FDA list gives ginger a pH of about 5.60–5.90.
Honey ranges in pH from 3.1 to 6.1, and some pathogens can grow at a pH as low as 3.7; honey is kept safe by its low water activity, not by its acidity.
JarAtlas has found no tested recipe for ginger and lemon in honey from a checked source.
